title: An LLM Compiler for Parallel Function Calling
technique: LLMCompiler: planner emits a function-call DAG, task fetching unit and executor run independent calls in parallel (with streaming planner)

optimized_metrics.evidence: the first framework to optimize ... the orchestration of LLM function calling that can not only ... improve latency and cost, but also accuracy

headline_claim.text: We observe consistent latency speedup of up to 3.7×, cost savings of up to 6.7×, and accuracy improvement of up to ∼9% compared to ReAct.

reported_metrics.where: Table 1 (end-to-end latency (s), speedup), Fig E.5 breakdown

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For all experiments, we have measured accuracy, end-to-end latency, as well as input and output token usage.
metric_definitions.notes: Latency of the whole function-calling task (planning + parallel tool execution + joiner); per-query average; not request rate-based. Includes planner overhead (slightly raises latency when there is no parallelism, App. E).

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The cost is computed based on the [number of input and output tokens]
metric_definitions.notes: Token-based API $ cost for GPT experiments.

tradeoff_acknowledged: Planner overhead slightly increases end-to-end latency on tasks without parallelizable calls.
hardware: API calls (GPT-3.5/4-turbo) and LLaMA-2 70B open-source serving (vLLM)
workloads: HotpotQA, Movie Recommendation, ParallelQA, Game of 24, WebShop
extractor_notes: Application-level (program) latency only; no TTFT/TPOT or throughput. Original ReAct latency not reported because of looping/early stopping. Mostly an LLM-agent framework paper; serving-layer relevance is as the PROGRAM_JCT-optimising orchestrator. Quality is also a headline.
